segments.en:
Parashas Kee Savoa teaches one to elevate every beginning to holiness, remember Hashem’s kindnesses, confess, give thanks, and serve with joy. Bikkurim, covenant, and blessing reveal that entering Eretz Yisrael depends upon remembrance, humility, prayer, and transforming abundance into avodas Hashem.

Entering the Land → bringing the first → remembrance and gratitude → confession and prayer → service with joy → blessing and covenant

The Arameans of the firstborn in confession say, "This is the loss of my father and he went down from Egypt." And our rabbis, the late Laban, sought to uproot everything. segments.en: There it is written: "Rejoice in Hashem, and let the tzaddik be glad." And it is written: "Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth be glad." And on this King Solomon, peace be upon him, said: "I will praise the joy that there is no better thing for a man than to rejoice." segments.en: And Hashem will make your plagues wondrous—great and faithful plagues, and evil and faithful illnesses. The root is emunah, and each person must search himself and strengthen himself in emunah. There are people who suffer illnesses and wondrous afflictions, and they suffer them only because emunah has fallen. Therefore the main healing is to seek and strengthen holy emunah, returning the mind and heart to Hashem.
